meta.title: FORGE — Powerlifting Strength, Periodization & Meet-Prep Library (Full Gym / Platform Equipment)

Novice.rpe_cap: RPE 6-7 max, no attempts above 80% e1RM
Novice.notes: Priority is bar-path and bracing technique on all three lifts before load matters at all. No max-effort singles, no accommodating resistance yet.

Beginner.rpe_cap: RPE 7-8 max, occasional work up to 85% e1RM
Beginner.notes: Standard linear progression on the three lifts; assistance work exists to fix the technical weak point that shows up on video, not to add general size.

Intermediate.rpe_cap: RPE 8 standard, RPE 9 on top single/triple once every 1-2 weeks
Intermediate.notes: Periodization structure starts to matter more than the exercise list — this is where linear progression typically stalls and block/wave structure earns its keep.

Advanced.rpe_cap: RPE 8-9 standard work, RPE 9-10 on top singles in-season
Advanced.notes: Individualize accommodating-resistance percentages and ME exercise rotation to the lifter's own strength curve and weak point (out-of-the-hole vs lockout, off-chest vs lockout, off-floor vs lockout).

Elite.rpe_cap: Autoregulated — written RPE is a floor, not a target
Elite.notes: Total weekly tonnage on the three lifts is usually the thing to cut, not add, once technique and the periodization structure are already sound — competitive results track recovery capacity as much as work done.

Linear Periodization.description: Same weekly exercise selection across a 4-week block; sets/reps decrease and intensity increases week to week, culminating in a top set/test week 4.
Linear Periodization.notes: Simplest structure to run and to coach — best default for Novice-Intermediate. Loses effectiveness once a lifter needs more than 4-6 weeks between meaningful PRs.

Block Periodization.description: Three sequential 4-week blocks — Accumulation (volume) → Strength (intensity) → Peak (near-competition specificity) — run as separate templates back to back.
Block Periodization.notes: Each block is programmed as its own template below; run Accumulation → Strength → Peak in order for a full 12-week cycle into a meet or a strength test.

Conjugate/Westside.description: Four fixed training days — Max-Effort Upper, Max-Effort Lower, Dynamic-Effort Upper, Dynamic-Effort Lower — run every week; the ME exercise variation itself rotates every 1-3 weeks rather than the program.
Conjugate/Westside.notes: Requires chains/bands and a lifter who can self-select an honest ME single — not recommended before Intermediate. ME exercise rotation is what drives long-term progress here, not a numbers-on-paper progression.

Wave/DUP.description: Three fixed training days per week — Heavy, Moderate, Light — each with a different rep/intensity target for all three lifts; the same three-day structure repeats with a small load increase each week.
Wave/DUP.notes: Daily Undulating Periodization keeps CNS freshness high by never stacking two heavy days back to back — well suited to lifters who respond poorly to a straight linear block.

Peaking / Meet-Prep.description: A taper block run in the final weeks before a competition (or a strength test) — volume drops and intensity rises every week, ending in an opener-selection week and a deload.
Peaking / Meet-Prep.notes: Openers are typically a weight the lifter could hit for a easy triple on a bad day (~90-92% of projected 1RM); second attempt ~95-97%; third attempt is the actual competition PR attempt. Never test a true 1RM in the gym during this block — the platform single is the first all-out attempt.

global_rules: Full commercial gym / powerlifting platform on-site — all barbell, specialty-bar, accommodating-resistance, and accessory equipment listed above is available without restriction; no equipment constraint applies to any template in this library.

The three competition lifts (Squat, Bench Press, Deadlift) or a direct variation of them stay the FIRST exercise trained in every session — assistance and accessory work always follows, never replaces, the competition-lift work for that day.

Technique standard comes before load at every level — a rep that would be a red-light call in competition (depth, chest touch/pause, lockout) does not count as a working rep, regardless of what the plate math says.

Deload every 4th week on Linear/Block/Wave styles: cut volume ~40-50% at reduced intensity. Conjugate style deloads by dropping DE-day bar weight to the bottom of the wave and skipping ME work for one week instead.

Progression rule: once every prescribed rep is hit at the given RPE/intensity for all sets, add load next session (Novice/Beginner) or next week (Intermediate+) rather than adding more sets — strength work prioritizes load over volume, the opposite of the hypertrophy-focused library.
Accommodating resistance (chains/bands) is Intermediate-level-and-up only — a lifter needs a stable, coached bar path before altering the strength curve of the lift makes sense.

Fatigue management across squat/bench/deadlift matters more in powerlifting than in any other strength sport in this library, since all three lifts share the same lower-back and grip recovery demand — heavy squat and deadlift work is never programmed on consecutive days.
Competition week: taper per the Peaking/Meet-Prep block below; the platform single on meet day is the first true 1RM attempt of the entire cycle — nothing in training should test a real max.
